name: ask_user
description: Ask the person who gave you the task a question and wait for the answer. Use it only when you cannot proceed without it, or to get explicit consent (for example to open a pull request with failing checks). Be specific. `question` is always required, with or without `choices`: it is the sentence the person reads first. Whenever the answer is one of a few options, pass `choices` and never write the options as a list in your text: the person gets one form with a list of options per question and answers them together; their answers come back as the result, so "yes" is never ambiguous. Give the form a short `title` and a `description` of why you ask (a sentence or two of plain text). Each entry of `choices` needs its own `question`; give every option a short `label` and a `description` that says what it means or what it costs, and mark the one you recommend with `recommended: true`. A question's `type` is `single` (radio buttons, the default; 2 to 12 options), `multiple` (checkboxes; 2 to 12; `min` and `max` say how many), `select` (a searchable list; 2 to 50 options), `images` (a deck of pictures; 2 to 16 options, each with `image` {sha256, alt}: the sha256 of an image file you shared in this conversation, never a URL) or `text` / `longText` (the person types the answer; no options). `help` is a line under the question, `default` is what is chosen at first, `allowOther` offers an "Other" the person can write, `freeInput` adds an "anything else" box. With a single possible answer, or none that you know, do not use `choices`: ask a plain question. There are at most 8 questions. An `id` or option `value` is 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits and `- _ . :`. Example: {"question": "A few things I need before I start.", "title": "Before I start", "description": "The migration depends on the database, so I need to know which one.", "choices": [{"id": "db", "question": "Which database?", "options": [{"label": "Postgres", "description": "Relational, the default", "recommended": true}, {"label": "MongoDB", "description": "Documents, no schema"}]}]} Without `choices` the question is plain text.

question.description: Required, even when `choices` is given: what you need to know, or the sentence that opens the form

title.description: The form's heading: a few words (with `choices`)

description.description: Why you are asking, in a sentence or two of plain text, no Markdown (with `choices`)

choices.description: Questions with fixed answers, asked together as one form (at most 8). Each needs `question` and, unless it is a typed answer, `options`. Omit for an open question.

id.description: A short id for the question (1 to 64 letters, digits, - _ . :), used in the answer; defaults to q1, q2, ...

help.description: A line under the question: what the options mean, or what the answer is for

type.description: How it is answered: single (radio buttons, the default), multiple (checkboxes), select (a searchable list), images (a deck of pictures), text (a short typed answer), longText (a longer one)

options.description: The answers to pick from, each a label or {value, label, description, image, icon, recommended}: 2 to 12 for single and multiple, 2 to 50 for select, 2 to 16 for images (each with an image); none for text and longText

value.description: A short id for the option (1 to 64 letters, digits, - _ . :); made from the label when omitted

label.description: The option's title: a few words

description.description: The option's subtitle: what it means or what it costs, in a short sentence

image.description: A picture of the option, for type "images": the sha256 of an image file you shared in this conversation, never a URL

alt.description: What the picture shows, in words

recommended.description: Mark this option as the one you recommend

multiple.description: Several options may be picked (the same as type "multiple"; with select and images it lets several be picked)

allowOther.description: Offer an "Other" the person can write

required.description: The person must answer this one (the default)

default.description: What is chosen at first: an option's value or label, or a list of them for several; the words a typed question starts with

min.description: The fewest options to pick, when several may be picked

max.description: The most options to pick, when several may be picked

freeInput.description: Add an "anything else" box to the form; its words come back as the note of the answer

submitLabel.description: The words of the button (at most 40 characters)
